     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	This plan delivers a CLI extraction script and a GUI "Text Only" tab that make LangGraph agent dialogue readable without parsing raw JSONL, sharing a common `.md` output format.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Add the `handleGetChunkText()` API handler in `api.ts` and its corresponding route in `server.ts` to serve extracted prose text via `GET /api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename/text`, with transparent `.md` file caching alongside the source `.jsonl`.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `mcp-server/gui/api.ts` — new `handleGetChunkText()` handler, `writeFile` import addition, `renderChunksToText` import
    15	- `mcp-server/gui/server.ts` — new route block for `/text` endpoint, `handleGetChunkText` import
    16	
    17	## Deliverables
    18	
    19	- `writeFile` added to the existing `import { rm, readFile, readdir } from 'node:fs/promises'` in `api.ts`
    20	- `renderChunksToText` imported from `'./chunk-renderer.js'` in `api.ts`
    21	- `handleGetChunkText(ledgerRoot, slug, filename, repoName?)` handler implementing:
    22	  - `assertSafeSlug(slug)` validation
    23	  - `CHUNK_FILENAME_RE` filename validation
    24	  - `resolveProjectStore` to resolve storage directory
    25	  - `.md` filename derivation from `.jsonl` filename (server-side, never from user input)
    26	  - Path prefix defence-in-depth check on the `.md` path
    27	  - Cache-first read: attempt `readFile(mdPath)` → return `{ content, cached: true }` on success
    28	  - Cache-miss path: read `.jsonl`, call `renderChunksToText()`, best-effort `writeFile(mdPath)` (ignore errors), return `{ content, cached: false }`
    29	  - `ENOENT` handling for both `.md` and `.jsonl` reads
    30	- Route in `server.ts` at `rest.length === 6, rest[3] === 'chunks', rest[5] === 'text'` following the existing `/rendered` route pattern with `resolveRepoName`, slug safety checks, and `handleGetChunkText` delegation

    34	- WP-002
    35	
    36	## Acceptance Criteria
    37	
    38	1. GET /api/projects/:repo/:slug/chunks/:filename/text returns { content: string, cached: boolean } with content-type: application/json
    39	2. When no pre-existing .md file exists, the endpoint extracts text, writes a .md file alongside the .jsonl (same directory, same base name), and returns { content, cached: false }
    40	3. When a pre-existing .md file exists (CLI-generated or prior access), the endpoint reads and returns it with { content, cached: true } without re-extracting
    41	4. A write error during .md caching does not propagate — the endpoint still returns the extracted content successfully
    42	5. Invalid filenames (path traversal attempts, non-.jsonl names) are rejected with a 404 response
    43	6. The .md filename is derived server-side from the validated .jsonl filename — never accepted from user input
    44	7. The route follows the same guard conditions as the existing /rendered route (SAFE_SLUG_REGEX checks, resolveRepoName, path prefix check)

     2	# WP-001: CLI extraction script and registration
     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	This plan delivers a CLI extraction script and a GUI "Text Only" tab that make LangGraph agent dialogue readable without parsing raw JSONL, sharing a common `.md` output format.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Create the standalone `scripts/extract-dialogue.js` Node.js ESM script that reads chunk `.jsonl` files, assembles streaming message fragments into prose turns, and writes `.md` files alongside the source. Supports single-file and directory batch modes, `--force`, `--dry-run`, and `--help`. Register it in `scripts/cli.js` as a hidden orchestrator command.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `scripts/extract-dialogue.js` — new file (Node.js ESM, stdlib-only)
    15	- `scripts/cli.js` — new `cmdExtractDialogue()` function and `COMMANDS` array entry
    16	
    17	## Deliverables
    18	
    19	- New `scripts/extract-dialogue.js` with:
    20	  - Shebang (`#!/usr/bin/env node`), doc comment, and usage block
    21	  - `parseArgs(argv)` — parses `--file <path>`, `--dir <path>`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, `--help`/`-h`, and a single positional argument (auto-detected as file or directory via `fs.statSync`)
    22	  - `discoverChunkFiles(target)` — returns `[target]` for a `.jsonl` file; returns all `*.jsonl` files in a directory (non-recursive, sorted alphabetically) for a directory target
    23	  - `parseJsonl(filePath)` — reads file, splits on `\n`, skips blank/malformed lines and the header line (`chunk_format` key), returns array of parsed objects
    24	  - `assembleText(entries)` — single-pass grouping of `AIMessageChunk` lines by `msg.id` (namespace-aware via `entry.ns`), concatenates `content[].type === 'text'` fragments per AI turn, accumulates per namespace key (`ns.length === 0` = outer/sole, `ns.length > 0` = inner), returns `{ outer: string, inner: string }`
    25	  - `extractFile(chunkPath, opts)` — orchestrates per-file: calls `assembleText()`, formats output (flat prose for single-section, `## Outer Agent` / `## Inner Agent` headers for dual-section), computes output path (`.jsonl` → `.md`, same directory), handles `--dry-run` (print path, skip write), handles skip-if-exists (unless `--force`), writes `.md` via `fs.writeFileSync`
    26	  - `main()` — parses args, discovers files, iterates with `extractFile()`, prints summary
    27	  - TTY-gated ANSI colours via `USE_COLOR = process.stdout.isTTY`
    28	  - `WORKSPACE_ROOT = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..')`
    29	  - No external dependencies — stdlib only (`fs`, `path`)
    30	  - Cross-platform paths (`path.join()`/`path.resolve()` only)
    31	- `cmdExtractDialogue(args)` in `cli.js` delegating via `runScript('node', [path.join(SCRIPTS_DIR, 'extract-dialogue.js'), ...args])`
    32	- `COMMANDS` entry immediately after `read-log`: `{ id: 'extract-dialogue', key: null, label: 'Extract chunk dialogue', category: 'Orchestrator', description: '...', helpVariants: [...], helpHidden: true, run: cmdExtractDialogue }`
    33	
    34	## Dependencies
    35	
    36	- None
    37	
    38	## Acceptance Criteria
    39	
    40	1. Running node scripts/extract-dialogue.js <chunk-file> produces a .md file in the same directory as the source .jsonl, with the same base name
    41	2. The .md file contains only assembled prose text from AI turns — no tool call JSON, no tool results — one paragraph block per AI turn
    42	3. For single-namespace chunk files, the output is flat prose without section headers
    43	4. For dual-namespace chunk files, the output has ## Outer Agent and ## Inner Agent section headers
    44	5. Running the script on a directory extracts all *.jsonl files in that directory (non-recursive, sorted alphabetically)
    45	6. Running with --dry-run prints the output paths without writing any files
    46	7. An existing .md file is not overwritten unless --force is passed
    47	8. Running with --help or -h displays usage information and exits
    48	9. node scripts/cli.js extract-dialogue <args> invokes the script correctly
    49	10. The COMMANDS entry uses key: null, helpHidden: true, and category: 'Orchestrator' — matching the read-log pattern
    50	
    51	## Active Pipeline Stages
    52	
    53	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    54	
    55	## Estimated Complexity
    56	
    57	High
    58	
    59	## Rationale
    60	
    61	Placing the extractor in `scripts/` alongside `read-log.js` keeps it discoverable and consistent. Writing `.md` files alongside `.jsonl` files (same directory, same base name) makes it trivially easy to open the readable version without a separate output path. Assembling streaming chunks in a single pass is sufficient — the files are small enough to fit in memory. An independent pure-JS implementation avoids build coupling with the TypeScript server-side renderer.
    62	
    63	## Rejected Approaches
    64	
    65	- *CLI imports from compiled dist (`mcp-server/dist/`)* — rejected because the compiled dist may be stale; an independent pure-JS implementation avoids build coupling while the shared format contract ensures compatible output.
    66	- *Separate `--output-dir` flag* — rejected because co-location of `.md` alongside `.jsonl` makes output obvious; a separate directory adds indirection without clear benefit.
    67	- *Stdout output instead of file writing* — rejected because the primary use case requires saved files (cache priming, repeated access); stdout can be used via shell redirection if ever needed.
    68	- *Always-overwrite default* — rejected because skipping existing files protects hand-annotated output; `--force` provides an easy override when regeneration is needed.
    69	- *Interactive menu entry in cli.js* — rejected because this matches the `read-log` pattern for secondary tooling; the command is not needed in the main interactive menu.
    70	- *Using `msg.tool_calls[].args` from final chunk for arg assembly* — rejected because the index-based accumulation of `tool_call_chunks[].args` is verified correct on real data; `tool_calls.args` remains `{}` throughout streaming.
    71	
    72	## Notes
    73	
    74	This WP is independent of all backend/frontend WPs (WP-002, WP-004, WP-005). The CLI and server-side renderer are independent implementations sharing a format contract — the Plan Context section of this WP and WP-002 both describe the same `.md` output format. Complexity is rated High due to the number of functions (5+ helpers) and the streaming fragment assembly logic, but this is justified — splitting the script into multiple WPs would create artificial boundaries since all functions are tightly coupled within a single file.
    75	
    76	**Code Observations:** `scripts/read-log.js` (the reference pattern) uses: shebang line, `import fs from 'fs'; import path from 'path';`, `WORKSPACE_ROOT = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..')`, TTY-gated colours via `USE_COLOR = process.stdout.isTTY`. In `scripts/cli.js`, the `COMMANDS` array starts at line 610; `runScript` and `SCRIPTS_DIR` are available in module scope (lines 26, 49). The `read-log` entry provides the pattern for `key: null`, `helpHidden: true`, `category: 'Orchestrator'`.

     5	# Development Guide
     6	
     7	## Workspace Directory Layout
     8	
     9	The root `package.json` depends on `@mistralys/cli-menu` (currently `^1.1.0` from npm).

    15	├── ai-insights/   ← this repository

    18

    20	
    21	## Pre-Commit Hook
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	node scripts/install-hooks.js
    25	```
    26	
    27	This enables a pre-commit guard that fails the commit if any generated persona file is stale (out of sync with its source template).
    28	
    29	## Global CLI (Optional)
    30	
    31	The root `package.json` declares a `bin` entry that maps the `ai-insights` command to `scripts/cli.js`. Running `npm link` from the repository root registers a global symlink, letting you invoke the CLI from any directory:
    32	
    33	```bash

    36	ai-insights sync-personas
    37	ai-insights doctor

    41	This is equivalent to `node scripts/cli.js <command>` in every respect.
    42	To remove the global symlink, run `npm unlink` from the `ai-insights/` root.
    43	
    44	## CI — Automated Quality Gate
    45	
    46	A GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on every push and pull request to `main`. It runs five independent jobs:
    47	
    48	| Job | What it checks |
    49	|-----|---------------|
    50	| `mcp-server-tests` | MCP server Vitest suite (Node.js 20) |
    51	| `orchestrator-tests` | Orchestrator pytest suite (Python 3.11) |

    53	| `manifest-validation` | `shared/workflow-manifest.json` schema + semantic checks |
    54	| `persona-build-check` | Detects stale generated persona output (`build-personas.js --check`) |
    55	
    56	Each job fails independently. npm and pip dependencies are cached to reduce cold-start times. All GitHub Actions refs are pinned to SHA digests (with inline version-tag comments) for supply-chain hardening. No deployment, artifact publishing, or release steps are included.
    57	
    58	## Shared Manifest
    59	
    60	`shared/workflow-manifest.json` is the single source of truth for the workflow specification: all 9 agent roles, 6 pipeline types, status enums, and workflow constants. All sub-projects derive their constant definitions from this file. It is validated by `shared/workflow-manifest.schema.json`.
    61	
    62	## Key Scripts (Advanced)
    63	
    64	> **For most operations, prefer the CLI menu:** `./menu.sh` (macOS/Linux) or `menu.cmd` (Windows). The table below documents the underlying `node` commands for CI, scripting, and advanced use.

    69	| `node scripts/sync-personas.js` | `./menu.sh sync-personas` | Build + deploy personas; validate frontmatter |
    70	| `node scripts/build-personas.js` | (part of setup/build) | Build personas only (no deploy) |

    72	| `node scripts/check-known-roles.js` | — | Verify role parity between personas and MCP server |
    73	| `node scripts/package-personas.js` | `./menu.sh package-personas` | Package standalone personas into distributable ZIPs |
    74	| `node scripts/bundle-docs.js` | `./menu.sh bundle-docs` | Compile project docs into bundles (e.g. for NotebookLM) |
    75	| `node scripts/cli.js ctx-generate` | `./menu.sh ctx-generate` | Generate context documentation via [CTX Generator](https://github.com/context-hub/generator) |
    76	| `node scripts/cli.js doctor` | `./menu.sh doctor` | Run all health checks; exits 1 on any failure |
    77	| `node scripts/cli.js install-mcp` | `./menu.sh install-mcp` | Register `central_pm` in VS Code user-level `mcp.json` via stable shim |
    78	| `node scripts/run-gui.js` | `./menu.sh gui` | Launch the MCP server GUI dashboard |
    79	| `node scripts/preflight-orchestrator.js` | `./menu.sh preflight` | Pre-flight readiness checks (venv, `.env`, dist, conflicts) |
    80	| `node scripts/run-orchestrator.js` | `./menu.sh orchestrator` | Launch the orchestrator (rebuilds MCP server if stale) |
    81	| `node scripts/kill-orchestrator.js` | `./menu.sh kill-orchestrator` | Detect and terminate stale orchestrator processes |
    82	| `node scripts/read-log.js` | `./menu.sh read-log` | Structured JSONL log reader — query, filter, and summarize orchestrator run logs |
    83	
    84	## Changelog Workflow

    86	This workspace uses a **hub-and-spoke changelog model**: each sub-project (`mcp-server/`, `orchestrator/`, `personas/`) has its own `changelog.md`, and the root `changelog.md` summarizes the highlights into versioned, Git-tagged releases.     11	For **local development** of `cli-menu` alongside `ai-insights`, clone it as a sibling directory and switch the dependency to a `file:` path:
    12	
    13	```
    14	parent/
    15	├── ai-insights/   ← this repository
    16	└── cli-menu/      ← optional sibling for local dev
    17	```
    18	
    19	The preflight bootstrap script (`scripts/preflight-bootstrap.js`) handles sibling linking automatically when both repos are present.
    20	
    21	## Pre-Commit Hook
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	node scripts/install-hooks.js
    25	```
    26	
    27	This enables a pre-commit guard that fails the commit if any generated persona file is stale (out of sync with its source template).
    28	
    29	## Global CLI (Optional)
    30	
    31	The root `package.json` declares a `bin` entry that maps the `ai-insights` command to `scripts/cli.js`. Running `npm link` from the repository root registers a global symlink, letting you invoke the CLI from any directory:
    32	
    33	```bash
    34	npm link          # register symlink (run once, from the ai-insights/ root)
    35	ai-insights       # opens the interactive menu
    36	ai-insights sync-personas
    37	ai-insights doctor
    38	ai-insights install-mcp --dry-run
    39	```
    40	
    41	This is equivalent to `node scripts/cli.js <command>` in every respect.
    42	To remove the global symlink, run `npm unlink` from the `ai-insights/` root.
    43	
    44	## CI — Automated Quality Gate
    45	
    46	A GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs on every push and pull request to `main`. It runs five independent jobs:
    47	
    48	| Job | What it checks |
    49	|-----|---------------|
    50	| `mcp-server-tests` | MCP server Vitest suite (Node.js 20) |
    51	| `orchestrator-tests` | Orchestrator pytest suite (Python 3.11) |
    52	| `ruff` | Orchestrator source linting (`ruff check src/`) |
    53	| `manifest-validation` | `shared/workflow-manifest.json` schema + semantic checks |
    54	| `persona-build-check` | Detects stale generated persona output (`build-personas.js --check`) |
    55	
    56	Each job fails independently. npm and pip dependencies are cached to reduce cold-start times. All GitHub Actions refs are pinned to SHA digests (with inline version-tag comments) for supply-chain hardening. No deployment, artifact publishing, or release steps are included.
    57	
    58	## Shared Manifest
    59	
    60	`shared/workflow-manifest.json` is the single source of truth for the workflow specification: all 9 agent roles, 6 pipeline types, status enums, and workflow constants. All sub-projects derive their constant definitions from this file. It is validated by `shared/workflow-manifest.schema.json`.
    61	
    62	## Key Scripts (Advanced)
    63	
    64	> **For most operations, prefer the CLI menu:** `./menu.sh` (macOS/Linux) or `menu.cmd` (Windows). The table below documents the underlying `node` commands for CI, scripting, and advanced use.
    65	
    66	| Script | Menu Equivalent | Purpose |
    67	|--------|----------------|---------|
    68	| `node scripts/cli.js` | `./menu.sh` | Interactive command center — menu-driven or direct CLI |
    69	| `node scripts/sync-personas.js` | `./menu.sh sync-personas` | Build + deploy personas; validate frontmatter |
    70	| `node scripts/build-personas.js` | (part of setup/build) | Build personas only (no deploy) |
    71	| `node scripts/build-personas.js --check` | — | Detect stale persona output (non-zero if stale) |
    72	| `node scripts/check-known-roles.js` | — | Verify role parity between personas and MCP server |
    73	| `node scripts/package-personas.js` | `./menu.sh package-personas` | Package standalone personas into distributable ZIPs |
    74	| `node scripts/bundle-docs.js` | `./menu.sh bundle-docs` | Compile project docs into bundles (e.g. for NotebookLM) |
    75	| `node scripts/cli.js ctx-generate` | `./menu.sh ctx-generate` | Generate context documentation via [CTX Generator](https://github.com/context-hub/generator) |
    76	| `node scripts/cli.js doctor` | `./menu.sh doctor` | Run all health checks; exits 1 on any failure |
    77	| `node scripts/cli.js install-mcp` | `./menu.sh install-mcp` | Register `central_pm` in VS Code user-level `mcp.json` via stable shim |
    78	| `node scripts/run-gui.js` | `./menu.sh gui` | Launch the MCP server GUI dashboard |
    79	| `node scripts/preflight-orchestrator.js` | `./menu.sh preflight` | Pre-flight readiness checks (venv, `.env`, dist, conflicts) |
    80	| `node scripts/run-orchestrator.js` | `./menu.sh orchestrator` | Launch the orchestrator (rebuilds MCP server if stale) |
    81	| `node scripts/kill-orchestrator.js` | `./menu.sh kill-orchestrator` | Detect and terminate stale orchestrator processes |
    82	| `node scripts/read-log.js` | `./menu.sh read-log` | Structured JSONL log reader — query, filter, and summarize orchestrator run logs |
    83	| `node scripts/extract-dialogue.js <target>` | — | Extract readable prose text from chunk `.jsonl` files; writes a `.md` alongside the source (same directory, same base name). Supports single-file and directory batch modes, `--force`, `--dry-run`, `--help`. Registered in `cli.js` as a hidden orchestrator command (`node scripts/cli.js extract-dialogue`). |
    84	
    85	## Changelog Workflow
    86	
    87	This workspace uses a **hub-and-spoke changelog model**: each sub-project (`mcp-server/`, `orchestrator/`, `personas/`) has its own `changelog.md`, and the root `changelog.md` summarizes the highlights into versioned, Git-tagged releases. See the Changelog Convention section in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for the full rules.
    88	
    89	When preparing a release, run the [changelog prompt](../.github/prompts/changelog.prompt.md) — it invokes the **Changelog Curator** agent to generate entries from Git history and update all four changelog files.
